title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks
abstract: Abstract Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO 2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four ‘AI-dreamt’ MOFs.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Long-Range and Short-Range Longitudinal Flow Decorrelations in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
abstract: The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) remains poorly constrained. Using a transport-model calculation of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ in relative pseudorapidity $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}$, we find two distinct initial-state components of flow decorrelation: a long-range component driven by the global geometry of participating nucleons and a short-range component reflecting local energy-deposition fluctuations. This short-range component extends to $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|\ensuremath{\sim}4$ and can be misidentified as final-state nonflow. For isobarlike nuclei with different shapes, the calculation predicts an experimentally testable fingerprint of this component: it dilutes the deformation contribution at small $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$, so that the ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ ratio between deformed and near-spherical systems, such as $\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{U}$-to-$\mathrm{Au}+\mathrm{Au}$, rises with $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$. Separating long- and short-range flow decorrelations from nonflow gives access to the longitudinal initial structure and dynamics of the QGP.

title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
abstract: Abstract Upon infection, arteriviruses, coronaviruses, and other nidoviruses transform endoplasmic reticulum membranes into viral replication organelles. These include large numbers of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) whose interior is considered the primary site of viral RNA synthesis. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. The discovery of DMV-spanning pore complexes in coronavirus-infected cells provided a plausible solution for this topological challenge. However, their structural organization, functional features, and evolutionary conservation across the nidovirus order, have remained unclear. Here, we investigate the macromolecular architecture of DMVs induced by two prototypic arteriviruses using cellular cryo-electron tomography. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
abstract: Abstract One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes. Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
